''The front page of the physics tools surveyed for [[The Principia Machina|the Principia Machina]]: twenty-two open-source programs (two of them run on the commercial Mathematica) for the three jobs between a theory and a measurable number &ndash; '''finding''' a law in data, '''deriving''' equations of motion from an action, and '''solving''' them &ndash; and for a fourth, '''checking''' a step by machine proof. Twelve come from the survey of 2026-09-26; ten were added on 2026-10-06. The tools are part 3 of the [[The Principia Machina/Research Toolkit|Research Toolkit]]. Choose the version written for you below; the full survey, the additions and the scores follow. The tools sit outside the machinery: [[The Principia Machina/TPS|the specification]] names none of them and the server, TPX, runs none of them; what reaches the wiki is a register record, checked like any other. Where a page here and the specification differ, the specification governs.''

== What the tools are for ==

Hamilton's principle reduces a physical system to one quantity, the action; the equations of motion follow from it, and the numbers follow from the equations ([[Hamilton's principle]]). Each tool takes one step of that road, or walks it backwards from data. A comparison with measurement comes last, after the work is finished, never during it.

<graphviz>

digraph road {
  rankdir=TB; compound=true; node [shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#eaecf0", color="#a2a9b1", fontcolor="#202122ff", fontname="Helvetica", fontsize=10]; edge [fontname="Helvetica", fontsize=9, color="#54595d", fontcolor="#202122ff"];

  subgraph cluster_find { label="FIND"; fontname="Helvetica"; fontsize=10; color="#ac6600"; F1 [label="PySR  AI Feynman\nPySINDy  Lagrangian networks", fillcolor="#ffedad"]; }

  subgraph cluster_derive { label="DERIVE"; fontname="Helvetica"; fontsize=10; color="#3366cc"; D1 [label="Cadabra2  ModelingToolkit.jl  SymPy\nSageMath  xAct  FeynCalc  FORM", fillcolor="#cedff2"]; }
  EQ [label="EQUATIONS OF MOTION", fillcolor="#cedff2"];
  subgraph cluster_solve { label="SOLVE"; fontname="Helvetica"; fontsize=10; color="#14866d"; S1 [label="FEniCS  Devito  Dedalus  DeepXDE  FiPy  Clawpack\nEinstein Toolkit  SpECTRE  QuTiP  Modelica", fillcolor="#cef2e0"]; }

}
</graphviz>

== How a tool's answer enters the Principia Machina ==

Each kind of output has one place to go. A law found in data starts a new container, because a container's kernel never changes. Equations derived from the kernel, and values computed from it, become register records. A comparison with a measured value is a record of its own, made only after the result it targets has landed. In every case the record is written out in full, its form is checked by TPX, and another agent reproduces it before it gains any standing.

<graphviz>
// Where each kind of output lands.
digraph lands {
  rankdir=LR; node [shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#eaecf0", color="#a2a9b1", fontcolor="#202122ff", fontname="Helvetica", fontsize=10]; edge [fontname="Helvetica", fontsize=9, color="#54595d", fontcolor="#202122ff"];
  T [label="A TOOL'S OUTPUT\nuntrusted until vetted", fillcolor="#ffedad"];
  K [label="A NEW KERNEL\nDRAFT UWC -> the gate ->\ndeclared by H-DECL", fillcolor="#cedff2"];
  L [label="RESULT, regime L\nan equation, with its ROLE;\na proof is its evidence", fillcolor="#cef2e0"];
  V [label="RESULT\na value, with its conditions\n(SITUATION records)", fillcolor="#cef2e0"];
  X [label="VERIFICATION\nthe difference from a\nmeasured value, afterwards", fillcolor="#cef2e0"];
  R [label="THE REGISTER\nchecked by TPX,\nreproduced by another agent", shape=box3d, fillcolor="#cef2e0"];
  T -> K [label="a law\n(FIND)"]; T -> L [label="equations\n(DERIVE)"]; T -> V [label="values\n(SOLVE)"]; T -> X [label="an outside\nvalue"];
  L -> R; V -> R; X -> R; K -> R [label="a new container's\nregister", style=dashed];
}
</graphviz>

Its scores are the survey's own judgments, not measurements; no rule of the Principia Machina reads them. The ten tools added on 2026-10-06 follow it, in their own section and their own matrix.''

'''The Principia Machina: Computational Tools Survey'''
[[Category:Principia Machina]] [[Category:Tools]]

== Overview ==
The [[The Principia Machina|Principia Machina]] (TPM) framework requires a versatile, high-precision computational ecosystem to evaluate candidate physical postulates against empirical and theoretical bounds. Following our baseline survey of acausal DAE modeling in [[The Principia Machina/Tools/Modelica|Modelica]], this survey expands the TPM computational arsenal across two crucial frontiers:
# '''Symbolic Regression & Lagrangian Discovery:''' AI-driven and evolutionary tools capable of discovering symbolic equations, conserved quantities, and Lagrangian densities directly from observational or simulated vacuum dynamics data.
# '''Advanced PDE & Field Dynamics Frameworks:''' Continuous field solvers, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), and spectral domain compilers capable of integrating spatial partial differential equations, hyper-dimensional differential forms, and spacetime manifolds.

== The additions of 2026-10-06 ==
Ten tools added by the [[The Principia Machina/Research Toolkit|Research Toolkit]]'s research pass of 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-06. Each covers something none of the twelve above does: a free reference algebra system (SymPy); tensor algebra for gravity, free-standing and on the commercial Mathematica (SageMath with SageManifolds; xAct); machine-checked proof (Lean with Mathlib and Physlib); quantum-field-theory algebra at interactive and industrial scale (FeynCalc, FORM); learning the Lagrangian or Hamiltonian as a network, with its structure built in (Lagrangian and Hamiltonian networks); a control model that assumes no action (PySINDy); spectral accuracy (Dedalus); and a second strong-field code (SpECTRE).

The scores are that pass's assessment, from the evidence cited on each tool's page, on the survey's four axes and its scale. They were made by a different hand from the survey's, so a difference of a point between one of the twelve and one of the ten means little. No rule of the Principia Machina reads them.
